chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Ali ibn al-Hakam and Safwan, from al-Ala', from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:

It is not befitting for a man to stay in Makkah for a year. I said, 'What should he do?' He (peace be upon him) said, 'He should move away from it. And it is not befitting for anyone to raise a structure above the Ka'bah.'
And it is reported that staying in Makkah hardens the hearts.
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on staying in Makkah for a year and raising buildings above the Ka'bah?
ai.summary: Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) advises against prolonged residence in Makkah for a full year, warning that it may harden the heart, while also prohibiting structures from exceeding the height of the Ka'bah to preserve its visual and spiritual prominence. This hadith, found in al-Kafi, reflects the scholarly tradition of balancing the sanctity of the holy city with the need for spiritual humility and avoiding stagnation in one place of worship.
